summary: Proof-worth registry entries owned by command-surface.

entries.contract: Source command manifests and generated compatibility artifacts stay in sync.
entries.worth: This is the cheapest proof that command metadata edits did not bypass generation.

entries.contract: The external-command v0 schema remains byte-exact frozen history while the active closed v1 schema, wire-v2 aggregate, exactly-one listen spawn registration, v1-only readers, generator-bound hashes, script targets, and help-manifest route coverage remain valid.
entries.worth: This catches frozen-history mutation, partial reader cutovers, open or unsafe spawn registration, and command schema drift without rebuilding or starting runtime services.

entries.contract: The stateless PNG comparator preserves byte-stable v1 no-write comparison, emits exact optional grayscale v2 artifacts through parent-identity-safe atomic publication plus a checked receipt, retains them on receipted expectation mismatch, reports cleanup failures, rolls back owned outputs on handled failure, and dispatches directly without capture or runtime services.
entries.worth: This proves pixel, artifact sample/hash, parser, direct-help topology, target and parent-identity safety, checked-receipt rollback, normal and failed rollback, unrelated-file preservation, expectation, resource-cap, and public-route behavior against production comparator and dispatcher sources without building or executing the repo binary.
entries.guard: compiles only disposable focused Swift harnesses and generates fixed PNG fixtures under a private temporary root; no capture, daemon, repo binary, or TCC

entries.contract: Direct and saved native perception terminate their exact child after owner, wrapper, or signal loss and cannot orphan a desktop capture.
entries.worth: This deterministically reproduces retained capture processes and unsafe live-daemon proof admission without invoking AOS, ScreenCaptureKit, or TCC.
entries.guard: uses disposable fake AOS children, exact PID assertions, bounded waits, and a preflight-only live-daemon fixture

entries.contract: Manifest-backed command routes dispatch through their external scripts and wrappers.
entries.worth: This catches route drift where generated command manifests still validate but runtime dispatch reaches the wrong implementation.
entries.guard: fails fast while a raw repo daemon is live, uses isolated state for daemon-sensitive checks, and holds the shared lockf process-cleanup boundary

entries.contract: External command wrappers reject malformed flags and arguments before falling through to native primitives.
entries.worth: This keeps parser failures explicit and prevents unknown input from reaching lower-level command adapters.
entries.guard: uses isolated AOS_STATE_ROOT and disables daemon autostart

entries.contract: Discoverable help, public command docs, parser errors, and generated command registry metadata stay aligned.
entries.worth: This is the broad command-surface guard that catches stale help or docs after manifest and adapter changes.

entries.contract: Repo-local GitHub helper command wrapping, argument rejection, CI inspection, and review-comment GraphQL behavior stay non-interactive and allowlisted.
entries.worth: This keeps GitHub workflow helper behavior out of the general router catch-all and prevents unsupported gh forms from slipping into maintainer automation.
entries.guard: uses a fake gh executable and no network

entries.contract: Repo-local GitHub helper subcommands stay dispatchable and discoverable through direct script help.
entries.worth: This keeps the sanctioned GitHub workflow subset discoverable without exposing unsupported gh prompts or hidden paths.
